references.text: Describes the same practice of burning the whole offering on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the Lord
The burnt offering is described as a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord
Parallel text where Moses burns the entire ram on the altar as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord
First time the expression 'pleasing aroma' (ריח ניחח) is used in the Bible, at Noah's offering
Fire offering to the Lord as a pleasing aroma; the same terminology is used
The daily burnt offering is described as a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord
Paul uses the same language about Christ's sacrifice as a pleasing aroma to God, fulfilling the Old Testament burnt offering
Paul describes the Philippians' gift as a pleasing aroma, an offering that God accepts with joy
Both verses describe different phases of the same consecration ritual (offering of the ram), where identical theological language links the parts into a unified sacrifice.
